drug_class: Vasopressin receptor antagonist (also called an aquaretic)
purpose: Tolvaptan is used to treat low sodium levels in the blood (a condition called hyponatremia) in certain patients, such as those with heart failure or liver or kidney problems. It is also used to slow down the worsening of a kidney disease called autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). It helps your body get rid of extra water without losing important salts like sodium.
how_it_works: Your body makes a hormone called vasopressin (or ADH) that tells your kidneys to hold onto water. Tolvaptan blocks the place where vasopressin attaches in the kidney, so your kidneys release extra water through your urine instead of keeping it. This helps raise your sodium levels or reduce fluid-filled cysts in the kidneys, depending on what you are being treated for.
common_side_effects: Feeling very thirsty, frequent urination (especially at night), dry mouth, feeling dizzy or lightheaded, headache, weakness, nausea, and increased blood sugar levels. You may notice you are urinating much more than usual — this is expected and means the medication is working.
warnings: This is a very important warning: Tolvaptan can cause serious liver damage, which can be life-threatening. You should not drink grapefruit juice while taking this medication. Your sodium levels must not rise too quickly, as this can cause serious brain problems. You should always have access to water and drink when you feel thirsty. Do not use this medication if you cannot feel thirst or cannot drink fluids freely. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, stomach pain, or unusual tiredness, as these can be signs of liver problems.
typical_dosing: For low sodium (Samsca): The usual starting dose is 15 mg once daily, and your doctor may increase it to 30 mg or up to 60 mg per day depending on how your body responds. For polycystic kidney disease (Jynarque): Dosing is split into two doses per day, often starting at 45 mg in the morning and 15 mg about 8 hours later, and may be increased over time. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, and never stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
